decision: Split rlsentry into a chain; first task is anon-probe (live black-box scan with anon key)
why: The request is a whole product; the black-box probe is what directly answers "verification, not reminders" and fixes the verdict/report model the rest builds on

decision: Write probe on by default but must never persist a row; uncertain → verdict unknown
why: Write exposure is half the CVE; scanning real prod data makes persistence the worst-case failure

decision: Reports never contain row values, only table, columns, row count
why: Exposed rows are likely third-party PII and reports land in CI logs

decision: No service-role key accepted in this task
why: Scan must see exactly what an outsider sees; avoids handling a secret

decision: Write probe: constraint-violation inference first, Prefer tx=rollback fallback, insert-then-delete forbidden
why: Owner chose A+B from the three options; C can leave rows in production when anon can insert but not delete

why: Owner confirmed restatement

decision: psycopg[binary] is the only runtime dependency; HTTP and HS256 JWT use the stdlib; jsonschema is a test-only extra
why: Ticket asks for few dependencies and allows a Postgres driver

decision: An interrupted run (SIGINT/SIGTERM) exits 2 after teardown, not 130
why: Keeps the brief's 0/1/2 contract (S-10)

decision: Teardown and sweep stop PostgreSQL before PostgREST
why: PostgREST ignores SIGTERM while a request is in flight; stopping postgres first ends both in ~0.05 s

decision: AnonChannel takes a port, not a URL, and its opener ignores proxy environment variables
why: Address can only be 127.0.0.1; attack requests must never go through an HTTP proxy

decision: Nonce check reads rlsentry_run.nonce over the sandbox's superuser connection and also requires both sandbox child processes to be alive
why: Design §2; liveness covers a server replaced after the build

decision: A 5xx from the REST layer raises AttackError (exit 2) instead of a protected verdict
why: A server error says nothing about the policies

decision: Stale sweep skips markers whose owning rlsentry process is alive, and signals a recorded pid only if its command line still names that run's dir
why: Two runs at once must not destroy each other's copy; guards against pid reuse

decision: No --backend flag and no Backend interface yet; the local backend lives inside sandbox.py
why: Only one backend exists in T-01; T-05 extracts the interface

decision: run(migrations, label) instead of run(MigrationsDir | Lab)
why: The lab is a migrations folder shipped in the package

decision: Seed fills only columns without defaults/identity; an unsupported column type leaves the table unseeded with a note
why: Minimal seed per ticket; the rest is T-03

decision: As root the run dir is created under /tmp and chowned to postgres, not under TMPDIR
why: TMPDIR may not be traversable by the postgres user

decision: Interrupt and kill -9 tests use a pg_sleep select policy to hold a run mid-attack instead of a test hook
why: Real mid-attack state without test-only product code

decision: The nonce test tampers rlsentry_run.nonce through Sandbox._conn, a private attribute
why: It is the superuser connection design §2 names; no public way exists

decision: The 127.0.0.1-address test replaces os.environ with a mapping where every name holds a decoy URL
why: The test cannot know which variable a regression would read

decision: Proxy and loopback-binding tests run rlsentry as a subprocess
why: Proxy env is read at import; listening sockets belong to a real run's children

decision: The text-report test pins the whole lab report body exactly
why: One worked example shows every line kind

decision: T-01 verified PASS at 5d96138 and merged into task/anon-probe (PR #3)
why: Fresh verifier session_01LCMZdmCqnfdzb8wvsFxA2R; risk high

decision: Re-cut: T-05 (docker backend) runs after T-02 and T-03, not in parallel
why: T-05 extracts a Backend interface out of sandbox.py, which T-02 and T-03 both change; parallel work would conflict throughout that file

decision: Pitfall candidate for retro: parallel builders shared the scratchpad (one overwrote the other's wrapper script) and test_teardown checks leftovers machine-wide, so it flakes when two builders run rlsentry at once
why: Reported by builder-T-02

decision: UPDATE/DELETE tried by first row's primary key, then without a filter; verdict from superuser before/after diff
why: A key filter makes PostgreSQL apply SELECT policies, so write-only policies change nothing by key; design §4 named only by-key

decision: Open for the owner: hosted Supabase may reject unfiltered UPDATE/DELETE (pg-safeupdate); not verified
why: Checking needs a live project (S-7)

decision: Restore = one snapshot of every public table after seeding; after each write attempt every table is rewritten with session_replication_role=replica
why: Swapping tables back would drop policies, grants and FKs; rewriting all also undoes cascades

decision: Sequences are not restored
why: Ids are not part of any verdict

decision: Attacker gets a narrow Inspector (rows, primary_key, fake_row), not the Sandbox or its connection
why: Design §1

decision: INSERT evidence is the new row read as superuser
why: S-4 asks for the row created

decision: UPDATE sets the first writable non-key column; known gap: unique first column reads protected (409)
why: Smallest choice covering the lab

decision: A table no fake row can be made for raises AttackError (exit 2)
why: Never call a table protected without attacking it

decision: Minimal auth.uid() (Supabase's definition) added to _SETUP_SQL
why: Ticket allows it; T-03 merges over it

decision: lab_owner_only policies have no TO clause
why: With 'to authenticated' the auth.uid() check would never be exercised

decision: auth.uid() test uses Sandbox._conn with SET ROLE anon (test-only SQL)
why: No REST path calls auth.uid() directly

decision: Suite and mutants run in a private pid namespace + /tmp

decision: Folded T-02 findings F1-F4 into T-04 (attacker area): untested 5xx branch, unexpected error exiting 1, 'not attempted' reported protected, unique-column update false negative
why: Same class as T-01's false all-clears; all in attacker.py/cli.py which T-04 owns next; F5 is covered by T-03's unseeded stop; F6 stays open for the owner

decision: T-03 verdict FAIL at 01b0f6a (D1 extensions not on search path for seeding/PostgREST; D2 psql meta-commands run on the host; D3 unexpected exception exits 1; D4 extensions schema and auth.users columns untested); fix round 1 started
why: Verifier reproduced each at level 5

decision: T-04's F2 (unexpected exception exits 1) moved into T-03 fix round 1; FK-409 delete and CHECK-rejected fake_row insert added to T-04
why: D3 names the same class in cli.py, so one fix covers both; the other two are attacker verdict classes like F1-F4

decision: Migrations applied by psql (--single-transaction, ON_ERROR_STOP) instead of psycopg
why: psql gives the line of the failing statement for every error; psycopg only for errors with a position

decision: The statement is named by its line number (where it ends), not quoted
why: Line plus psql's own LINE context is enough to find it; quoting a multi-line statement adds noise

decision: auth.uid/role/jwt read only request.jwt.claims; T-02's legacy request.jwt.claim.sub fallback dropped
why: PostgREST 12 sets only request.jwt.claims; the ticket names that setting; nothing could test the fallback

decision: auth.users is a subset of Supabase's columns, with defaults for aud, role and metadata
why: Enough for references and the usual trigger fields; GoTrue normally fills these

decision: No USAGE grant on extensions and no PostgREST db-extra-search-path; USAGE on auth kept
why: Policies and defaults store resolved objects, so mutants showed no difference; auth USAGE is needed for a direct auth.uid() call (T-02's test)

decision: auth.users is seeded because tables reference it, not listed explicitly
why: An unreferenced auth.users has no effect on an anon attack

decision: Tables in other schemas that public tables reference are seeded too
why: Otherwise a public table with an FK to them could not be seeded

decision: FK cycles broken by leaving a nullable key null; a cycle of NOT NULL keys falls to name order and fails visibly
why: The usual way out of mutually referencing tables; never a silent partial copy

decision: CHECK values from the constraint's own constants (strings; numbers n, n+1, n-1), at most 50 tries per row
why: Covers in(...), between, < and > without evaluating expressions; the same bound as the brief's value search

decision: A table counts as seeded if it has any rows; rows that already exist (migration seed data, triggers) are kept and fake rows are still tried
why: Brief: migrations' seed data is used too; a trigger-filled table must not stop the run

decision: A nullable column of an unsupported type is left null instead of blocking the table
why: Only a NOT NULL column without a value makes a table unseedable

decision: Arrays of generated types are now generated; T-02's unfillable fixture switched from text[] to point
why: text[] is common in Supabase apps; the fixture still needs a type that cannot be filled

decision: fake_row (write attacks) uses T-03's generators; a rolled-back trial insert only on tables with CHECKs
why: A trial insert uses up an identity value, which would shift T-02's pinned evidence ids

decision: Suite and mutants run in a private pid namespace and /tmp
why: The machine-wide residue checks flake while another builder runs rlsentry

decision: Migrations no longer go through psql: each file is split into statements by rlsentry (psql's rules: quotes, E'', dollar quotes, nested comments, parens, BEGIN ATOMIC) and sent through psycopg, one transaction and one connection per file
why: The verdict asked for no client that interprets backslash commands; the Supabase CLI also splits client-side and sends statements to the server; a connection per file keeps a migration's SET out of seeding

decision: Error line = line of the error's position when Postgres gives one, else the failing statement's first line (psql gave the line where the statement was sent)
why: More exact for multi-line statements; the line is now the only thing the splitter changes, since the server accepts a mis-split chunk

decision: Search path set once as the server default (postgres -c search_path) instead of ALTER DATABASE, plus PostgREST db-extra-search-path "public, extensions" and usage on schema extensions for anon/authenticated/service_role
why: ALTER DATABASE missed connections already open (the seeding one); a server default reaches every connection; PostgREST drops a schema its role cannot use

decision: Catch-all in cli.main: any other Exception prints "the run failed unexpectedly (Type: message); the copy was torn down" and exits 2, without a traceback
why: S-10 reserves exit 1 for exposed; teardown already runs through the Sandbox context manager

decision: auth.users gets the Supabase columns triggers typically read (instance_id, invited_at, confirmation_sent_at, recovery_sent_at, last_sign_in_at, is_super_admin, phone_confirmed_at, confirmed_at generated, banned_until, is_sso_user, deleted_at); token and secret columns left out
why: Smallest set that covers typical handle_new_user triggers; none of the left-out columns is read by triggers in Supabase's examples

decision: psql dropped from the required binaries
why: Nothing uses it any more

decision: iso.sh refuses a checkout under /tmp instead of supporting it
why: It mounts a fresh /tmp, which would hide such a checkout; the repo's normal places are outside /tmp
